notes: Assertions are objectively checkable statements for grading. Mechanics evals (route C) are fully scriptable via persian_lint; translation evals mix scriptable checks (entities/digits present) with judgment checks (idiomatic, register, no AI tells).

evals.prompt: Translate this into Persian in a literary, first-person memoir register: "I left India in 1964 with a certificate in commerce and the equivalent, in those days, of ten dollars to my name."
evals.expected_output: Idiomatic literary Persian. 'to my name' rendered with the Persian idiom «دار و ندار» (e.g. «همهٔ دار و ندارم ده دلار بود»), not the flat «ده دلار پول» and not an invented referent like a bank account; 1964 -> ۱۹۶۴; faithful; mechanically clean (ZWNJ, «»).
assertions: Output is Persian prose in a literary/memoir register.
'1964' is rendered with Persian digits «۱۹۶۴».
'ten dollars to my name' uses «دار و ندار» or an equivalent 'all I owned' idiom; it does NOT add a referent absent from the source (bank account, wallet) and is NOT the flat «ده دلار پول».
No Arabic letters ي/ك remain; «» guillemets used for any quotes; ZWNJ used where required.

evals.prompt: Translate to Persian and keep the dialogue casual and colloquial, the way a real person speaks: "Go on, now," he said. "This is grown-ups' time. Go read one of your books."
evals.expected_output: Colloquial spoken register (e.g. «برو دیگه، یالا» / «بزن بچاک»), dialogue tag flattened to «گفت», spoken verb forms, not a flat literal calque.
assertions: Dialogue reads as natural spoken/colloquial Persian, not a word-for-word calque («برو دیگر، حالا» fails).
The tag 'he said' is flattened to «گفت» (no ornate manner verb).
Quoted speech uses «» guillemets and is mechanically clean.

evals.prompt: Translate this Persian sentence into natural English: «همزمان با صدای بوقِ مایکروفر، برق رفت و موسیقی قطع شد.»
evals.expected_output: Faithful, natural English; 'the lights/power went out' and 'the music stopped/cut out'; meaning preserved.
assertions: Output is natural English (not a calque).
'برق رفت' becomes 'the lights/power went out' (not 'electricity left').
'موسیقی قطع شد' becomes 'the music stopped/cut out'.
No content added or dropped vs. the Persian source.

evals.prompt: Fix the Persian formatting/typography in this text (don't translate it): او مي رود و كتاب ها روي ميز است ، و بزرگ ترين آرزو همين بود 1964 .
evals.expected_output: Mechanics only via persian_lint: ي->ی, ك->ک, ZWNJ for «می‌رود»/«کتاب‌ها»/«بزرگ‌ترین», 1964->۱۹۶۴, spacing around «،» and «.» fixed. No translation, no re-wording.
assertions: Contains «می‌رود» joined with ZWNJ (U+200C), not «می رود» and not «میرود».
Contains «کتاب‌ها» with ZWNJ.
Contains «بزرگ‌ترین» with ZWNJ.
No Arabic ي or ك remain (all converted to ی/ک).
'1964' converted to «۱۹۶۴».
No space before «،» or the final period; wording is otherwise unchanged (no translation).

evals.prompt: I'm writing in Persian and need a natural equivalent for the idiom 'it cost an arm and a leg', please don't translate it word for word.
evals.expected_output: An idiomatic Persian equivalent such as «کلی آب خورد» / «خرج روی دستم گذاشت», with a note that a literal calque is wrong.
assertions: Gives an idiomatic Persian equivalent (e.g. «کلی آب خورد» / «خرج روی دستم گذاشت»), not a literal body-parts calque.
Explicitly flags that a word-for-word translation would be wrong.

evals.prompt: Translate this faithfully into Persian: "They opened a bottle of wine and drank until he got drunk."
evals.expected_output: Complete, accurate rendering: شراب and مست both present; nothing omitted or softened.
assertions: Contains «شراب» (wine), not omitted, swapped for juice, or softened to «نوشیدنی».
Contains «مست» (drunk), not omitted or softened.
Meaning is complete and uncensored relative to the source.

evals.prompt: Normalize this Persian but keep the numbers in Latin digits, it's going into a code sample: نسخه 2 و سال 1990 و كتاب ها روي ميز.
evals.expected_output: ك->ک, ي->ی, «کتاب‌ها» ZWNJ, spacing fixed, but digits stay Latin (2, 1990) because the user asked (persian_lint --digits keep).
assertions: Arabic ك/ي converted to ک/ی and «کتاب‌ها» joined with ZWNJ.
Latin digits 2 and 1990 are PRESERVED (not converted to ۲/۱۹۹۰), honoring the explicit request.
No translation performed.

evals.prompt: Clean up the typography of this text, don't translate it: او گفت "سلام" و رفت . كتاب ها روي ميز بود ; ساعت 10 صبح بود ؟ Then he asked, "Are you sure?" and left.
evals.expected_output: Persian part: straight quotes -> «…»; ; -> «؛»; ? -> «؟»; ك/ي fixed; «کتاب‌ها» ZWNJ; 10 -> ۱۰; spacing normalized. English sentence keeps its own comma, quotes, and question mark.
assertions: Persian straight quotes "سلام" converted to «سلام».
';' converted to «؛» and the Persian '?' to «؟», with correct spacing (no space before, one space after).
ك->ک, ي->ی; «کتاب‌ها» joined with ZWNJ; '10' -> «۱۰».
The English sentence 'Then he asked, "Are you sure?" and left.' is unchanged (Latin comma, quotes, and question mark kept).
Persian content is preserved verbatim (no translation or rewording).

evals.prompt: Translate to Persian: 'It snowed three feet that winter.'
evals.expected_output: Faithful Persian; because the text has a meaningful measurement and no unit policy was given, the skill should ASK or offer options (metric / keep original / both) rather than silently converting. If converted, three feet ≈ «حدود یک متر» (P19).
assertions: Either asks the user about unit policy OR explicitly offers the options (metric / original / both) before committing; does not silently drop the measurement.
Any conversion is numerically sensible (three feet ≈ one meter) and consistent.
The rest of the sentence is idiomatic Persian.

evals.prompt: This Persian paragraph sounds like ChatGPT wrote it. Rewrite it so it sounds like a person wrote it, keeping every fact: «لازم به ذکر است که این محصول دارای سه ویژگی کلیدی می‌باشد. این محصول نه تنها سریع، ساده و کارآمد است، بلکه توسط تیمی متخصص طراحی شده است. در نهایت، این محصول می‌تواند نقش مهمی در بهبود تجربهٔ کاربری ایفا کند.»
evals.expected_output: Plain modern Persian with the same facts: three features, fast/simple/efficient, designed by a specialist team, improves user experience. No «لازم به ذکر است», no «می‌باشد», no «دارای», no «توسط» passive, no «نه تنها … بلکه», no «در نهایت», no «نقش مهمی ایفا می‌کند». No new facts.
assertions: Output contains none of: «لازم به ذکر است», «می‌باشد», «دارای», «توسط», «نه تنها», «در نهایت», «ایفا».
All facts survive: three features; fast, simple, efficient; a specialist team designed it; it improves user experience.
No fact, number, or claim is added that the source does not contain.
Uses simple verbs («دارد», «است», «طراحی کرده‌اند») and reads as natural modern Persian.

evals.prompt: Translate to Persian: "The teachers were dragged out of the school and shot. 'Isn't that the day the war started?' she asked. 'Yes,' he said."
evals.expected_output: Impersonal active for the passive («معلم‌ها را … بیرون کشیدند و تیرباران کردند»), and «چرا» (not «بله») as the affirmative answer to the negative question.
assertions: The passive 'were dragged out and shot' is rendered as third-plural active («…را بیرون کشیدند و … کردند»), not «کشیده شدند / کشته شدند».
The answer to the negative question is «چرا» (possibly «چرا، همان روز است»), not «بله».
Names/facts intact; dialogue uses «» and reads as spoken Persian.
